claims.text: Electroless copper pre-coating of tungsten particles before sintering will increase the thermal conductivity of a W–Cu composite.
The copper pre-coating will allow the composite to retain its mechanical durability.
The copper pre-coating will allow the composite to retain its irradiation resistance.
A pre-deposited copper layer will produce a more coherent interface between the tungsten and copper phases.
A pre-deposited copper layer will produce a less defective tungsten–copper interface.
The pre-deposited copper layer will minimize oxide formation at the tungsten–copper interface.
The pre-deposited copper layer will minimize interfacial gaps.
The copper coating will improve electron transmission across the tungsten–copper interface.
The copper coating will improve phonon transmission across the tungsten–copper interface.
The copper coating will reduce tungsten–copper interfacial thermal resistance.
Metallurgical continuity supplied by the copper coating will preserve the composite's mechanical strength.
Metallurgical continuity supplied by the copper coating will preserve resistance to radiation-induced microstructural degradation.
Relative to an otherwise identical composite made with untreated tungsten particles, the modified composite will show a measurable increase in thermal conductivity.
The predicted benefit is expected from room temperature through the high operating temperatures typical of heat-dissipation and fusion-reactor joint applications.
The predicted benefit is expected under moderate neutron irradiation typical of fusion environments.
Changes in processing or exposure to extreme conditions may alter the predicted benefits.
